Our results indicate that plasma effects can mimic part of the shadow size shift, but the distinct charge response of CWG offers a potential observational route for separating conformal gravity signatures from environmental propagation effects.

title: Proximity-Induced Giant Majorana Spin Response in a UTe$_2$-Metal Film Heterostructure
summary: We establish an experimentally accessible route to identifying Majorana surface states through their intrinsic Ising spin response, using UTe$_2$ as a concrete platform. The key is to extend the Majorana correlations into an adjacent metallic film via the superconducting proximity effect, thereby making the otherwise surface-localized response accessible to NMR measurements. Remarkably, disorder further sharpens the Majorana signature: impurity scattering suppresses the conventional $p$-wave proximity correlations while preserving the Majorana contribution, yielding a giant Ising-anisotropic enhancement of the NMR relaxation rate. This approach also offers a powerful means to distinguish among candidate pairing symmetries.

title: Development of a real-time FPGA-based CNN trigger operating on full-granularity calorimeter images
summary: We present a real-time field-programmable gate array (FPGA) implementation of a convolutional neural network (CNN) for event classification on full calorimeter images that retain crystal-level shower information. To meet the resource and latency constraints of trigger electronics, the network parameters and hidden activations were quantized to 8 bits with quantization-aware training, and a lossless space-to-depth reorganization rearranged the input image into fewer spatial positions, reducing the estimated CNN inference latency by more than an order of magnitude. The approach was evaluated with the J-PARC KOTO detector, recorded data, and data-acquisition (DAQ) constraints as a benchmark, targeting the online separation of the rare $K^{0}_{L}\rightarrowπ^{0}e^{+}e^{-}$ decay from its dominant $K^{0}_{L}\rightarrowπ^{+}π^{-}π^{0}$ background. As a proof of principle, the firmware was implemented and validated on an AMD Versal Premium VPK120 evaluation board. On 100,000 test events, inference on the board rejected $(99.34\pm0.04)\%$ of the recorded background sample enriched in $K^{0}_{L}\rightarrowπ^{+}π^{-}π^{0}$ decays at a nominal $K^{0}_{L}\rightarrowπ^{0}e^{+}e^{-}$ efficiency of 95%, with a measured CNN inference latency of 17.9 $μ$s. Combining the measured image-assembly and CNN inference latencies with the estimated link-transfer and score-return times gives a projected end-to-end latency of 25.9 $μ$s, within the adopted 32 $μ$s DAQ latency budget. These results demonstrate the feasibility of using full-granularity calorimeter images for CNN-based event selection that achieves high background rejection while keeping the trigger latency within tens of microseconds.

title: Trace Relations and Partition Functions
summary: In general trace relations appear in finite $N$ matrix models and collective field theories. They lead, as was established previously, to reductions of large $N$ Hilbert spaces. Even more importantly they induce the appearance of a whole class of new (miraculous) states whose number grows exponentially in $N^2$. In this work we discuss their relevance to finite $N$ thermodynamics and the role they play in constraining the partition functions of finite $N$ theories.

title: Optimization of the second Robin eigenvalue on a planar exterior domain under fixed area constraint
summary: We consider the Robin Laplacian on a planar exterior domain with a negative boundary parameter. For a negative boundary parameter of a sufficiently large absolute value this operator has at least two negative eigenvalues below the bottom of the essential spectrum. We prove that under a fixed area constraint and convexity assumption on the bounded complement of the exterior domain the second Robin eigenvalue is maximized by the exterior of the disk. The inequality is strict for every exterior of a non-circular domain whenever the comparison disk has a negative second eigenvalue. The proof modifies the parallel-coordinate method by allowing the angular phase of a trial function to vary with the distance from the boundary. This result resolves the first item in a 2024 conjecture by the authors under an additional convexity assumption. Relaxing the convexity and the perimeter constraint remain open problems.

title: Reconstruction of the Riemann tensor from causal order and element counts
summary: A causal set is a locally finite partially ordered set. Causal set theory proposes such discrete structures as a basis for spacetime physics. Connecting this description with continuum physics requires recovering the geometric quantities used in general relativity and controlling the errors introduced by discreteness. Here, with dimension and sampling density specified, we construct approximate normal coordinates, estimate parallel transport, and recover the full Riemann tensor from causal order and element counts. For samples embedded in a fixed smooth spacetime and satisfying stated uniform counting assumptions, we prove a uniform curvature error bound that tends to zero as the sampling density increases.

title: Mesons, Confinement, and Complexity: A Krylov Space Perspective on the Long-Range Ising Chain
summary: We investigate the interplay between confinement and Krylov complexity in the long-range transverse-field Ising chain, where power-law interactions $\sim 1/r^α$ generate an effective confining potential between domain walls without an explicit symmetry-breaking field. Using the time-averaged Krylov state complexity after a quench as a diagnostic, we find that the complexity is strongly suppressed and only weakly system size-dependent at small $α$ and small transverse field $h_x$, where confinement is strongest, and crosses over to rapid growth at larger $α$, where it increases with system size. Within the confined regime, the oscillation frequencies of the complexity agree with the meson masses of an effective two-kink model, with the dominant frequency growing linearly with the lightest meson mass and the time-averaged complexity decreasing approximately as its inverse square. We further study operator Krylov complexity at finite temperature using the Wightman inner product. At low temperature, it exhibits bounded oscillations that directly encode the meson spectrum, whereas this structure is progressively washed out as the temperature increases. These results identify Krylov complexity as a spectroscopic probe of interaction-induced confinement and reproduce, in a microscopic lattice model, the hallmarks of Krylov complexity identified in confining field theories.

title: Probing Charged Higgs Bosons through $H^\pm \to W^\pm A$ Decay in the Type-I Two-Higgs Doublet Model
summary: A light pseudoscalar lighter than the 125 GeV Higgs boson remains allowed within the type-I Two-Higgs Doublet Model (2HDM), consistent with current collider constraints, including Higgs signal strength measurements and direct searches for additional Higgs bosons. At the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), the light pseudoscalar $A$ can be pair-produced through the undetected decay of the Standard Model-like Higgs boson, $h_{125} \to AA$, when this channel is kinematically accessible (i.e., $m_A < m_{h_{125}}/2$). For the charged scalar $H^\pm$, once open, the bosonic decay channel $H^\pm \to W^{\pm(*)} A$ naturally dominates over the fermionic $H^\pm \to τ^\pmν$ and $H^\pm \to tb$ channels, while relaxing the existing $H^\pm$ limits. As a result, we propose searching for the charged Higgs boson through $H^\pm \to W^{\pm(*)} A$ in the $4b+2j+\ellν$ final state. This channel is particularly sensitive to moderate-to-large $\tanβ$ values and provides an excellent complementary probe to searches based on fermionic $H^\pm$ decays at the LHC. Our collider analysis demonstrates that this channel can probe a substantial region of the type-I 2HDM parameter space at the high-luminosity LHC.

title: The heterotic superpotential and the alpha' expansion
summary: We study the role of the Hull connection in the heterotic superpotential for N=1 d=4 vacua. The integrand is defined in terms of H, which is in turn defined in terms of a gravitational Chern--Simons coupling involving H. We show this recursive structure is key to W reproducing some of the ten--dimensional supersymmetry conditions written down by Bergshoeff--de Roo through α'^3. With this evidence in hand we make some observations about extending some of the tensor equations of Hull and Strominger to all orders in α'.

title: Quaternionic Buzano-Dragomir Inequality and Deutsch Entropic Uncertainty Principle
comment: 14 Pages; 0 Figures, Quaternionic Kraus Conjecture and Quaternionic Crouzeix Problem are added
summary: We show that the Buzano-Dragomir inequality holds for quaternionic Hilbert spaces. Using this generalization, we derive the Dragomir inequality for the quaternionic numerical radius and Deutsch entropic uncertainty principle for quaternionic Hilbert spaces.

title: Improved constraints on higher-derivative effective field theory extensions of general relativity with GW230627_015337
summary: Gravitational-wave (GW) observations of binary black holes provide a powerful probe of general relativity (GR) in the strong-field regime. In effective field theory (EFT) extensions of GR, higher-curvature operators modify the binary dynamics and introduce corrections to the inspiral phase. In this work, we consider two parity-even cubic-curvature couplings and one quartic-curvature coupling, whose leading phase corrections enter at 5PN, 6PN, and 8PN order, respectively. We incorporate these corrections into the individual multipoles of the \texttt{SEOBNRv5HM\_ROM} waveform using the flexible theory-independent framework, allowing higher-order modes and the full inspiral-merger-ringdown signal to be used in the analysis. We first perform a Fisher-matrix analysis of 92 binary-black-hole events selected from a parent sample of 273 events in the public LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA catalogs. GW230627\_015337 provides the tightest forecast constraints on all three EFT couplings and is therefore selected for a full Bayesian analysis. The posterior distributions are consistent with GR, with all three couplings consistent with zero at 90\% credibility. The corresponding one-sided 90\% upper limits on the characteristic length scales are \(17.1\), \(11.1\), and \(18.3\,\mathrm{km}\). The log Bayes factors of the three EFT models relative to GR range from \(-5.49\) to \(-2.51\), favoring GR under the adopted priors. These bounds probe higher-curvature length scales at the level of \(10\)--\(20\,\mathrm{km}\) and are numerically tighter than representative previous inspiral and ringdown constraints, although differences in the models and analysis assumptions should be taken into account.

title: Universal Scaling of Conditional Mutual Information in Classical Stochastic Dynamics
summary: Conditional mutual information (CMI) characterizes dependence between two regions conditioned on an intervening buffer. Its characteristic decay length, the Markov length, has recently been identified as a diverging length scale at mixed-state phase transitions. Here, we investigate CMI dynamics in one-dimensional classical stochastic models and propose a universal scaling form for systems whose Markov length diverges with time. We derive this form in the inactive phase of parity-conserving directed percolation, where domain-wall coarsening generates a growing length scale and a self-similar probability distribution. We introduce a Hankel-based truncation scheme that enables matrix-product-state simulations at long times and over large spatial regions. Using this method, we verify the proposed scaling both in the inactive phase and at the nonequilibrium critical point, where the dynamical critical exponent governs Markov-length growth. More broadly, the same scaling form captures cases in which collective inference sets the diverging Markov length. Despite these distinct mechanisms, the CMI between fixed microscopic regions exhibits a common scaling dimension of two. Finally, we extend this framework to temporal CMI, establishing an analogous relation between the strength of conditional dependence in time domain and its characteristic memory time.

title: Phenomenology of strangeness-changing two-body currents in antineutrino scattering
comment: 33 pages, 7 figures, 13 tables. Companion of arXiv:2610.32375
summary: Antineutrinos produce hyperons without kaons through Cabibbo-suppressed quasi-elastic scattering on a single nucleon. A two-body current acting on a correlated nucleon pair, nubar [NN] -> l+ Y N', gives the same hyperons plus a second nucleon. A companion paper constructs this current without fixing its size. StrangeMC, the only generator with the channel, set it to a flat 15% of the quasi-elastic hyperon cross section. We determine the ratio f = sigma_2p2h/sigma_QE of the two-body to the quasi-elastic hyperon cross section on carbon versus antineutrino energy, and the detector signatures of two-body events. The strange two-body current and its non-strange counterpart are computed on the same nucleon pair. Their ratio is converted into f with the Valencia non-strange 2p2h and quasi-elastic cross sections for carbon, assuming that nuclear effects missing from the pair are common to both. Under this assumption f rises from 0.14 at 0.6 GeV to 0.20-0.22 at 2-5 GeV. Averaged over the Booster antineutrino spectra it is 0.15-0.17, close to the 15% placeholder, which StrangeMC now replaces with f(E). The largest evaluated uncertainty comes from separating the two-body current from one-body production followed by rescattering: across the separation prescriptions explored, f at 1 GeV ranges from 0.12 to 0.22. Interference with one-body production is not calculated and could be as large as the two-body rate. In a simulated SBND antineutrino-mode exposure on argon with the carbon f, two-body events are about 11% of events that produce a strange hadron. They supply more than a quarter of the kaon-less Sigma+ events used to tag hyperon charge exchange, partly as Sigma+ made at the weak vertex. They reconstruct 12-30% low in energy under the quasi-elastic hypothesis. After final-state interactions half of them have a proton above 40 MeV at the vertex, against a fifth of quasi-elastic events.

title: The Wess-Zumino Action of the Conformal Anomaly
comment: 27 pages, 2 figures, Contribution to String Theory and Particle Physics: A Themed Issue in Honor of Professor Ignatios Antoniadis on the Occasion of His 70th Birthday
summary: The complete Wess-Zumino (WZ) action and stress-energy tensor (SET) of the conformal anomaly in both two and four dimensions is given. This local effective action is expressed in terms of a single scalar Nambu-Goldstone `conformalon' field $\varphi$, parametrizing the local abelian Weyl group of conformal transformations that act transitively on the spacetime metric. Satisfying WZ consistency, and equipped with a variational principle for $\varphi$ that determines the conformal transformation $g_{μν}\!\to\!g_{μν}e^{-\varphi}$ to an associated spacetime with no anomaly, the WZ action resolves the conformal gauge fixing ambiguity of earlier methods of `integrating the anomaly.' In $D\!=\!2$ the WZ action is the local form of the Polyakov action, whose massless $\varphi$ propagator describes a correlated two-particle scalar intermediate state in the SET polarization function $\langle TT\rangle$. The imaginary part of this polarization obeys a UV finite sum rule, becoming a Dirac $δ$-function at zero energy for conformal quantum fields, demonstrating the infrared origin of the anomaly, while the real part becomes the light cone propagator of $\varphi$. Although the $\Box R$ term in $D\!=\!4$ corresponds to a cohomologically trivial cocycle, it also arises from the IR limit of massless quantum fields, independently of UV physics, and contributes to the WZ action for low energy gravity. Analogous to the WZ action for pseudo-Goldstone mesons in low energy QCD from the axial anomaly, the WZ action for the conformal anomaly provides a Nambu-Goldstone scalar field for macroscopic gravity, in addition to the metric of classical general relativity.

title: Parametrized Jacobian Problem over $\mathbb{C}^n$ and its Complete Resolution
summary: We formulate a parametrized Jacobian Problem over $\mathbb{C}^{n}$ by incorporating independent scale parameters into the linear part of a polynomial map via polar decomposition. We prove that requiring the Jacobian determinant to remain constant uniformly across the parameter space decouples the Jacobian equation into a system enforcing the vanishing of all principal minors of the perturbation matrix. This system strictly forces lower triangularization up to variable permutations, establishing a necessary and sufficient condition for polynomial invertibility and providing an explicit, canonical scheme for constructing the inverse map in every dimension.

title: Impact of deformation parameters on the greybody factor and Joule-Thomson expansions of Schwarzschild-AdS black hole
summary: This paper investigates the greybody factor and Joule-Thomson expansion of deformed Schwarzschild-AdS black hole models. We constructed the Klein-Gordon equation into a Schrödinger-like wave equation using tortoise coordinates and derived the exact effective potential. Also, we analyzed its behavior under varying physical parameters, including deformation parameters, mass and angular momentum. In this case, our results illustrate that increasing the deformation parameter enhances the effective potential, significantly impacting the absorption and scattering of massless scalar fields. It is noted that the Schwarzschild black hole effective potential is greatly increased when the deformation parameter is present. Near the event horizon, we found that waves behave differently, with higher-frequency waves more easily penetrating potential obstacles and lower-frequency waves bouncing off them. Furthermore, we investigated the thermodynamic characteristics of black holes using the Joule-Thomson expansion, detecting isenthalpic curves that indicate heating and cooling zones controlled by pressure and temperature changes. In this context, we tested the influence of deformation black hole parameters; the isenthalpic curves are enhanced by increasing the deformation parameters and the black hole mass.

title: The Glass Transition: From Competing Theories to Discriminating Tests
summary: The dramatic slowing down of liquids approaching the glass transition remains unresolved, partly because competing theoretical explanations are difficult to discriminate. Indeed, several mature, contrasting frameworks account for the main features of glassy phenomenology, making agreement with familiar observations a weak basis for identifying the microscopic mechanism responsible for the slowdown. Recent numerical advances are changing this situation in two complementary ways. Deep equilibration extends controlled equilibrium studies into regimes previously accessible only by extrapolation, allowing established predictions to be stress-tested over a broader dynamical range. At the same time, new numerical methods increasingly provide direct access to theory-specific quantities such as configurational entropy, static lengths, elastic properties, and local activation barriers. I discuss how these developments constrain thermodynamic, facilitation-based, elastic, and excitation-based descriptions. The emerging picture is not yet a unique theory, but a set of increasingly discriminating tests that can reveal where apparently successful laws cease to be universal and identify the microscopic ingredients that causally control the activation barrier.

title: Improved nonflow control for multiparticle correlators and system-size-dependent evolution from OO to Pb--Pb collisions at the LHC
summary: Multiparticle correlations of event-plane angles, known as symmetry plane correlators (SPCs), and correlations of anisotropic flow amplitudes of different harmonics, known as symmetric cumulants (SCs), help constrain the initial conditions and the transport properties of the system formed in heavy-ion collisions. Such multiparticle correlations are robust against nonflow biases in heavy-ion collisions; however, in small systems the nonflow contribution is sizeable and can distort SPCs and SCs at low multiplicity, mimicking a flow-like signal. Evidence of nuclear-geometry-induced collectivity in light-ion collisions, such as OO and Ne--Ne, has been established at the LHC. Measurements of SPCs and SCs in these systems, and their comparison to heavy-ion collisions, can therefore clarify the system-size dependence of these correlations and the strength of nonlinear mode coupling. In this work, an improved nonflow subtraction framework based on multiplicity reweighting ($\czero$) and $v_1$-estimator-based ($\cone$) scaling is validated for selected SPCs and SCs using a controlled toy model and the \textsc{Pythia~8~Angantyr} model, where collective flow is absent by construction. We find that $\cone$ provides the more reliable nonflow control and apply it to predict the SPCs and normalized SCs in OO collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=5.36$~TeV with the \textsc{ampt} string-melting model. The results are compared with published Pb--Pb measurements from ALICE and from \textsc{ampt} as a function of midrapidity charged-particle multiplicity $\langle N_{\rm ch}\rangle(|η|<0.5)$, placing light- and heavy-ion systems on a common system-size axis.

title: Wilson loops of Chern-Simons-matter Theories with one parameter and Picard-Fuchs equations
summary: Extending our previous work, we investigate Wilson loops of flavored Chern-Simons theory and ABJ theory by the use of Picard-Fuchs equations. The singularity structure of the equations is analyzed in detail, and local solutions around the singularities are determined. Each theory has one parameter, and the parameter dependence of the Wilson loops is also determined. In flavored Chern-Simons theory, we find an interesting phase transition. For $n$-times-wound Wilson loops, we determine their $n$-dependence by using a recursion relation obtained in our previous work.

title: Evaluation of a Double Integral with Exponentials and Two Generalized Laguerre Polynomials and Its Associated Moments
summary: We analytically evaluate in terms of finite sums, the following definite improper integral, which appears in the quantum field theoretical calculation involving elementary charged particles having charge $\pm e$ in presence of a constant external magnetic field $\mathbf{B}=B\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ $$ I_{abln}^{μ_1\dotsμ_r}(\mathbf{q}_\perp,|eB|) = \int\!\!\dfrac{d^2k_\perp}{(2π)^2}k_\perp^{μ_1} \dots k_\perp^{μ_r} \exp \bigg(-\frac{\mathbf{k}_\perp^2+\mathbf{p}_\perp^2}{|eB|}\bigg) L^a_l \bigg(\frac{2\mathbf{k}_\perp^2}{|eB|}\bigg) L^b_n \bigg(\frac{2\mathbf{p}_\perp^2}{|eB|}\bigg)\bigg|_{\mathbf{p}_\perp=(\mathbf{q}_\perp+\mathbf{k}_\perp)} $$ where $μ_i \in \{1,2\}$, $l\ge 0$, $n\ge 0$ and $L_l^a(x)$ are the generalized Laguerre polynomials. We also provide explicit expressions of the result up to the fourth moment i.e. $r=4$, which are sufficient for most of the field theoretical calculations.

title: Novel topological subclasses of a magnetic black hole in causal nonlinear electrodynamics
summary: By treating black-hole states as topological defects in thermodynamic parameter space, we investigate a static, asymptotically flat magnetic black holes in Einstein gravity coupled to causal nonlinear electrodynamics. Using the generalized off-shell free energy and Duan's $φ$-mapping topological current theory, we analyze the physical single-horizon sector in the canonical ensemble. We identify four representative defect-curve profiles, including realizations of the conjectured $W^{0+\leftrightarrow1-}$ class and $\overline{W}^{1-}$ subclass, as well as a new thermodynamic topological subclass, $\overline{W}^{0+\leftrightarrow1-}$. This new subclass features paired generation and annihilation points, with unstable innermost and outermost branches. As the auxiliary inverse temperature increases, the system evolves from two equilibrium states to three and then back to one, with an unstable small-black-hole defect entering through the physical lower boundary and changing the global topological number from $W=0$ to $W=-1$. This boundary-induced change signals a thermodynamic topological phase transition. These results show that the same inverse-temperature endpoint behavior and winding-number sequence from small to large black holes can accompany different defect evolution, highlighting the role of the physical horizon boundary in thermodynamic topological classification. More broadly, this causal nonlinear-electrodynamics black-hole family provides a setting for discovering further defect structures and thermodynamic topological phase transitions.

title: STEM-Bank-26: An Open Dataset of Analytical Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy Images and Spectra
summary: Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) is a versatile, multi-modal method for studying materials at the nanoscale. It integrates multiple signal sources to provide atomic resolution imaging alongside spectroscopy for elemental composition and electronic structure. Despite its utility, few datasets spanning multiple years of data have been published. We introduce STEM-Bank-26, a 929 GB open dataset of 37,921 STEM images that spans 1,095 material samples across 1,499 sessions and includes energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) or electron-energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) data for 65.5% of sessions. We extract microscope control trajectories by comparing metadata between sequential images and provide tools for building similar datasets from archival data. To our knowledge, this is the largest openly available dataset that integrates experimental STEM, EDS and EELS data across a broad distribution of samples and sessions.

title: What the Primary Lund Plane Omits: A Model-Stitching Diagnosis of a Jet-Tagger Representation Gap
summary: Lund-plane and Particle Transformer (ParT) jet taggers can differ in performance because one representation is weaker, or because a weaker downstream computation reads an adequate one. Standalone performance cannot separate these. Model stitching can: it links the frozen early layers of one network to the frozen late layers of another through a single trained linear map. As a positive control we use an incomplete Lund representation, the primary declustering branch, whose deficit is known independently. Stitched into ParT's downstream, it reaches a background rejection at least as much as its own downstream recovers, yet far below ParT's background rejection: the deficit is representational, not computational. A hypergraph reader over splitting triplets does no better, ruling out higher-order correlations as the cause. The gap is invisible in AUC, which stays within 1\% of its target value, and appears only in background rejection at low signal efficiency. It localizes to 0.6\% of background jets, at and above the top mass, with more constituents but fewer primary splittings than typical background. Rebuilding the representation on the full Cambridge/Aachen declustering tree repairs the deficit as predicted: standalone rejection rises, closing 72\% of the gap. Masking nodes at inference shows the repaired network still relies almost entirely on the primary branch; the secondary splittings make the representation learnable rather than supplying information it reads. Along the primary branch, the widest-angle splitting, near the top and $W$ opening angles, is worth nearly twice a random one. For quark/gluon tagging the primary branch is far less deficient, retaining 77.6\% of ParT's rejection (46.9\% for top), and the full tree closes only 33\% of the gap (72\% for top).

title: The Disordered Universe 2025: Open Effective Field Theories
comment: 67 pages, 13 figures, 1 table. A chapter to be published by Springer Lecture Notes in Physics
summary: Effective field theories (EFTs) offer a powerful method to unify diverse models under a small set of control parameters, allowing systematic expansions around well-established theories. While these techniques were traditionally developed for particle physics experiments with clean, isolated initial states, realistic macroscopic environments are often noisy and dissipative. Recognising the limitations of traditional EFTs has recently sparked intense progress at the interface of high-energy physics and condensed matter. These developments motivate a new approach to gravitation and cosmology, one that models the gravitational sector as evolving in the presence of an unobservable medium. Open Effective Field Theories provide a systematic, controllable framework for this endeavour. This chapter presents this versatile framework and illustrates how the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism captures the influence of unknown environments, manifesting as dissipation and noise, on observational probes. These notes are based on a series of lectures held during the La Ricotta Summer School "The Disordered Universe 2025" from 21 July to 1 August 2025.

title: Analytic Bootstrap Solution for Quantum Mechanics on a Circle
comment: 6 pages including appendix; 2-column format; Numerical procedure implemented in Python in the ancillary Jupyter Notebook "Analytic_Bootstrap.ipynb"
summary: We solve the Schrödinger equation for a particle in the circle with a quantum mechanical bootstrap method. The main idea is that in physical situations one needs solutions of the recursion relations for the Fourier coefficients of the measure that vanish exponentially fast. We show that this results in a (generalized) continued fraction representation of the solution. The solution is an analytical function of the couplings and the energy. We also show how one this method directly computes the density of states and checking that the answer is physical is reduced to checking an inequality for a single variable. We also show how to reconstruct the wave function and how to extract the quasimomentum of the particle as a function of the energy. We illustrate our solution in the simplest case of the Mathieu equation, where we show that the method can easily resolve exponentially small bands in the band spectrum.

title: Realistic neutron stars in the constant-Q branch of f(Q) gravity
summary: We investigate the hydrostatic equilibrium and global structure of neutron stars within symmetric teleparallel gravity, where gravitational interactions are mediated by the non-metricity scalar $Q$. Working within the metric-affine formulation, we adopt the regular, constant-$Q$ branch ($Q = Q_*$) of $f(Q)$ gravity, which preserves regularity at the stellar centre while maintaining explicit dependence on the non-linear functional form through $f(Q_*)$ and its derivatives. We propose three novel non-linear $f(Q)$ extensions: (i) a Born-Infeld-inspired model, (ii) a Hu--Sawicki analogue, and (iii) a Tsujikawa-inspired model. Incorporating state-of-the-art realistic unified equations of state, namely GPPVA(DD2) and SLy4, we numerically solve the modified Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations and evaluate stellar stability via the Harrison-Zel'dovich-Novikov criterion. The Born-Infeld and Hu-Sawicki analogues smoothly recover the general relativistic limit as their control parameters increase, predicting stellar radii for low-mass objects ($M < 2.0\,M_\odot$) that match observational constraints from X-ray binaries and GW170817; however, their maximum masses remain capped below $2.43\,M_\odot$ (DD2) and $2.06\,M_\odot$ (SLy4). Conversely, the Tsujikawa-inspired model significantly stiffens the effective gravitational coupling, accommodating massive compact objects up to $\sim 3.36\,M_\odot$ and offering a viable physical origin for the $2.59_{-0.09}^{+0.08}\,M_\odot$ secondary object in GW190814, albeit at the expense of overpredicting radii for typical low-mass neutron stars. These contrasting behaviours demonstrate a key phenomenological complementarity between maximum mass and radius bounds within the constant-$Q$ framework, highlighting the utility of multimessenger observations in constraining non-linear non-metricity gravity.

title: A Hybrid Brownian Dynamics-kinetic Monte Carlo Framework for Coupled Magnetic and Rotational Dynamics of Nanoparticles
summary: Simulating the coupled magnetic and rotational dynamics of suspended magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) over experimentally relevant timescales remains computationally demanding, particularly under low-frequency alternating magnetic fields. Here, we develop a hybrid Brownian Dynamics--kinetic Monte Carlo (BD--kMC) framework that combines thermally activated magnetic switching with particle rotation while retaining local fluctuations of the magnetic moment. These fluctuations are incorporated through Metropolis Monte Carlo (MC) sampling, allowing the moment to depart from the energy minima and thereby capturing the thermally averaged anisotropy torque that governs particle rotation. To preserve the distinction between local fluctuations and magnetic reversals, a barrier-trapping criterion confines MC trial moves to the current energy well, leaving thermally activated switching to the kMC process. For non-interacting single-domain MNPs, comparison with stochastic Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert (LLG) simulations demonstrates agreement in the equilibrium torque and stationary easy-axis orientation, including the field-driven transition from predominantly perpendicular to parallel alignment. The resulting BD--kMC framework provides an efficient approach to coupled magnetic and Brownian Dynamics, reducing the computational cost of exploring the long timescales relevant to low-frequency magnetic applications.

title: An end-to-end framework for uncertainty-aware validation of generative models
summary: Density estimation with generative models is a common task in the physical sciences, for example in background estimation in particle physics. Existing machine learning techniques, however, lack methods to quantify uncertainties that can be propagated into a statistical test. That limits the validation of generative models to standard goodness-of-fit tests, in which the generative model is treated as exact (point-null hypothesis). But a model fitted to a finite training set is never exact, so if its uncertainties are neglected, any sufficiently powerful goodness-of-fit test will eventually reject it once the test set is large enough to resolve this estimation error. We propose SIGMA, an end-to-end framework combining density estimation with principled uncertainty quantification. We use Gaussian mixture models, for which uncertainties are tractable, and further construct a new goodness-of-fit test in which these uncertainties are profiled as nuisance parameters to account for the statistical error of the fit, promoting the conventional point-null test to a composite one. A rejection then signals genuine mismodeling rather than a test set large enough to resolve the error of the fit, provided the propagated uncertainties faithfully cover that error. We demonstrate the framework on a controlled two-dimensional toy model and on a collider physics benchmark modeling the QCD background process. With uncertainties included, the same model can be trusted on test sets up to an order of magnitude larger than the standard test allows. Our work thus provides a statistically grounded basis for a robust use of generative models in the physical sciences.

title: The Disordered Universe 2025: Statistical Systems Out of Equilibrium
comment: 41 Pages, 10 Figures. A chapter to be published by Springer Lecture Notes in Physics
summary: These lecture notes provide an introduction to quantum spin glasses, with a particular emphasis on their application to open problems in cosmology and holography. Focusing on the spherical $p$-spin model, we develop a complete and self-contained analysis of its thermodynamic and dynamical properties. We introduce the replica method, discuss both replica-symmetric and one-step replica symmetry-broken solutions, and characterise the resulting glassy phase. The framework is then extended to the quantum model, where we study the emergence of slow dynamics and the role of quantum correlations through Euclidean and real-time correlation functions. Finally, we explore how concepts such as replica symmetry breaking and disorder naturally arise in cosmological and holographic systems related to black hole fragmentation, highlighting spin glass models as useful theoretical laboratories for these phenomena. These notes are based on a series of lectures held during the La Ricotta Summer School: The Disordered Universe 2025 from 21 July to 1 August 2025.

title: An algebraic characterisation of $n$-qubit pure-state invariants
summary: We study the set of $n$-qubit pure quantum states. Specifically, we consider their incarnation as density matrices in Bloch representation. Building on prior work, we define a family of quadratic functions in Pauli expectation values, and fully characterise all instances that result in state-independent purity constraints. The resulting family of pure-state invariants is surprisingly rich in structure, with strong ties to the geometry of symplectic polar spaces. After charting the general landscape, we define a sub-family of pure-state invariants that satisfies the dynamical constraint of being stable under state update. We prove that it corresponds with (different embeddings of) symplectic Lie algebras $\mathfrak{sp}(2^{n-1})\subset\mathfrak{su}(2^n)$, which admit a generating set of Pauli operators. We carefully distinguish the symplectic case from its orthogonal counterpart, using the Arf invariant of quadratic refinements of the symplectic form on the projective Pauli group, which we further identify with quaternionic structures on $\mathbb{C}^{2^n}$ that are both generated by and restricted to Pauli operators. As a consequence of this analysis, we reveal previously largely overlooked structure in the $n$-qubit Pauli group. We highlight this in a number of examples. We characterise all state-independent uncertainty relations in variance for Pauli observables, as well as all Pauli channels for which the output fidelity and output purity are state-independent. We further show that the orbits of the projective stabiliser groups of pure-state invariants, which for $n\geq2$ are proper subgroups of the Clifford group, form complex projective state $2$-designs, while their unitary lifts form symplectic $2$-designs.

title: Primordial black holes from a type-IIB/F theory inflaton potential
summary: We study the possibility of the formation of primordial black holes (PBHs) using an inflaton potential constructed by stabilizing all Kähler moduli employing both the perturbative and non-perturbative corrections in the large volume scenario in type-IIB/F string theory. We further introduce a small perturbation in one of the Kähler moduli that modifies the existing potential in the field space. The effective correction in the moduli space is made by introducing a localised Gaussian bump, which induces an ultra-slow-roll feature in the inflaton potential during the early cosmological inflation. The evolution of the amplitude of the curvature power spectrum is solved numerically by using the Mukhanov-Sasaki equation, with Bunch-Davies initial conditions. The inclusion of the Gaussian bump produces a sustainable enhancement in the amplitude of curvature power spectra around $k\sim 1.12 \times 10^{9} Mpc^{-1}$ for the formation of PBHs. The abundance of PBHs ($f_{PBH}$) is calculated using the Press-Schechter formalism for different values of critical density contrast and presented in the background of contemporary $f_{PBH}$ bounds and checked for viability with existing microlensing bounds, corresponding to a mass value $10^{-6}M_\odot$ for $δ$ threshold value $δ_c=0.439$. The Hawking temperature and evaporation time are also determined for these black holes and found to be of the order of $2.78\times 10^{-15}$ GeV and $8.5\times10^{38}$ Gyr, respectively. The enhancement of curvature power spectra lies in the sensitivity region of the SKA observations, suggesting an indication that scalar-induced gravity waves may be probed in future observations.

title: A 3D-$Δ$PDF-like measure for hidden anisotropy in disordered materials
summary: We introduce a simple correlation function for quantifying hidden local anisotropy in disordered materials. Developed in analogy with the three-dimensional difference pair distribution function (3D-$Δ$PDF), our approach identifies structural correlations that are lost through averaging over bulk symmetry. The same approach might be applied to models of disordered crystals, amorphous materials, and liquids alike.

title: Momentum-space entanglement and mutual information in Kaluza-Klein reduction
summary: In theories with compact extra dimensions, the four-dimensional effective description is obtained by Kaluza-Klein reduction. The state available to a four-dimensional observer is the reduced density matrix obtained by tracing the higher-dimensional vacuum over the tower of massive modes, and it need not be pure. In this paper we study the momentum-space entanglement of this state for a five-dimensional scalar on $M_4\times S^1$ with a cubic or quartic self-interaction. We compute, at leading order in the coupling, the mutual information $I_n$ between the zero modes below a resolution scale $μ$ and a single Kaluza-Klein level $n$. When the zero modes couple linearly and without derivatives to pairs of tower modes, $I_n$ falls as $1/m_n$, where $m_n$ is the mass of level $n$. In the cubic theory, this tail is independent of the ultraviolet cutoff, with coefficient $(μR)^2/1024π^3$ for compactification radius $R$, and the mutual information with the whole tower grows logarithmically with the number of levels. In the quartic theory, the tail is masked by states containing additional hard quanta, which make $I_n$ depend on the cutoff. Compared with the corrections the tower makes to low-energy amplitudes, which are dominated by the lightest levels and captured by local operators, the mutual information with the tower is not dominated by any finite set of levels and arises from the time-nonlocal part of the effective action. The local four-dimensional effective theory therefore describes the low-energy observables of the reduced system but not its state. Unbroken supersymmetry cancels the vacuum energy of the compactification but not the mutual information, which at leading order is a sum of squared amplitudes.

title: The Keller problem for the lowest positive eigenvalue of Dirac operators with Lorentz scalar potentials
summary: We study the Keller problem for the Dirac operator $\mathcal{D}_m - Vβ$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and minimize its lowest positive eigenvalue over all potentials $V$ with prescribed $L^p$ norm. We prove that optimal potentials always exist and that the corresponding eigenspinors solve the nonlinear Soler equation. This provides a variational proof of existence of solitary waves for this equation. We prove that there are no zero modes for such operators in dimensions $1$ and $2$, and conjecture that zero mode may exist in dimension $3$. In dimension $d = 2$, we provide numerical evidence that the optimal potentials concentrate on flower-shape regions, which are not necessarily radial, showing that Faber--Krahn type results may fail for such Dirac operators. In dimension $1$, all quantities are explicit.

title: Self-gravitating Schrödinger--Poisson Solitons in Curved Spacetime
summary: We formulate a description of self-gravitating Schrödinger--Poisson (SP) solitons in curved spacetime using a local inertial frame centered on the soliton. In the weak-field and non-relativistic regime, the effect of the background spacetime is incorporated into the SP equations through an effective tidal potential determined by the spacetime curvature. We apply this framework to a soliton moving along a circular equatorial geodesic around a Kerr black hole. The tidal field contains stationary and time-dependent quadrupolar components, which induce a deformation of the soliton and an associated mass quadrupole moment. We formulate the quadrupolar response in terms of the tidal deformability and the dimensionless Love number. We then estimate the gravitational radiation associated with the rotating deformed soliton and evaluate the corresponding characteristic strain for representative soliton sizes and orbital radii. A comparison with representative sensitivity curves of planned space-based gravitational-wave detectors identifies parameter regimes in which the estimated characteristic strain may lie within their sensitivity ranges. Our framework provides a systematic basis for investigating the tidal response of self-gravitating bosonic solitons in black-hole spacetimes and their potential gravitational-wave signatures.

title: Coulomb- and exchange-driven redistribution of spectral correlations
summary: Electronic correlations reorganize not only the energies of individual electronic states but also the collective structure of the spectrum. Here, first-principles density functional theory calculations combined with random-matrix spectral statistics are used to examine this reorganization in gamma-Ce within a static spin-polarized DFT+U+SOC description. We distinguish the effects of the Coulomb interaction U from those of the exchange interaction J by analyzing nearest-neighbor spacings, reduced spacing ratios, band velocities, and band curvatures across the Ce-4f manifold. Increasing U does not produce a monotonic transition between Poisson- and Wigner-Dyson-like statistics; instead, the region of strongest level repulsion migrates across the 4f manifold as the interaction increases. Exchange produces a qualitatively different response. At fixed U, strongly repulsive and strongly clustered spectral regions coexist within the same 4f manifold even while the total spin moment and 4f occupation remain nearly unchanged. The clustering persists after resolving the spectrum into its dominant j = 5/2 and j = 7/2 components and differs strongly between calculations having the same numerical value of U-J. Within the present DFT+U+SOC description, the spectral response therefore depends on the separate Coulomb and exchange interactions and cannot be represented completely by a single effective U-J parameter. These results show that energy- and character-resolved spectral statistics expose correlation-driven electronic reorganization that is hidden by conventional integrated observables.

title: Another Brick in the Wall: Spectral Form Factor of Normal Modes in Horizonless Geometries
summary: We compute the normal mode spectrum and its spectral form factor for a probe scalar wave in smooth horizonless backgrounds. We first consider the BTZ black hole with a brickwall that hides the near-horizon region, which has recently been proposed as a toy model for a finite-temperature semiclassical black hole microstate. In this setup, the spectral form factor may or may not have a linear ramp, depending on the details of the brickwall construction. However, we argue that even in cases that do show a ramp, this ramp does not originate from level correlations associated with quantum chaos. Then we calculate the normal mode spectrum for a genuine microstate geometry (superstratum) and find evidence of chaos, both with a ramp and level repulsion. We conclude that the eigenvalue spectrum of normal modes can indeed serve as a tool for investigating the quantum dynamics of fuzzballs; however, the brickwall models are incapable of capturing this phenomenon.

title: Elasticized magnetohydrostatics
summary: The modern approach to modeling equilibria in stellarators features two blind spots: lack of foundational agreement between theory and computation, and inability to reliably explore economically-attractive high-$β$ concepts. These blind spots originate at a technical level from lack of a useful existence theory for the partial differential equations believed to describe equilibria, and from the encumbrance of crude, inflexible models for the topology of the confining magnetic field. This Article proposes the first stellarator equilibrium model that rigorously guarantees existence of an equilibrium with any chosen magnetic topology. It completely separates determination of the magnetic topology from the equilibrium existence question, and thereby enables importing realistic tearing physics into equilibrium computations. The new model replaces the standard plasma potential energy functional with its ensemble average over rapid kinetic-scale fluctuations. Averaging ``elasticizes" the potential by energetically penalizing separation of field lines. The elasticized potential's super-linear dependence on plasma strain embodies a phenomenological model for profile stiffness, and plays an essential role in the existence theory.

title: Can One Hear the Absence of a Singularity?
summary: One of the central expectations of quantum gravity is the resolution of the curvature singularities predicted by General Relativity, potentially giving rise to effective black-hole geometries that are regular inside the horizon. We show that, for a very broad class of regular black holes including several known solutions, the quasinormal-mode spectrum in the large-overtone limit differs discontinuously from that of a Schwarzschild black hole, even when the regularization parameter is arbitrarily small. The real part of the quasinormal frequencies vanishes asymptotically, rather than approaching a nonzero constant, as generically occurs in General Relativity and other theories predicting black holes with curvature singularities. The asymptotic black-hole spectrum thus retains a distinctive imprint of singularity resolution. We establish these results analytically through a systematic formulation of the monodromy method and confirm them numerically. We interpret this phenomenon as a manifestation of black-hole spectral instability, whereby arbitrarily small deviations from vacuum General Relativity produce nonperturbative changes in the large-overtone spectrum.

title: Ensemble-dependent condensate statistics and correlations in an ideal Bose gas
summary:
The choice of statistical ensemble has a measurable impact on the statistical description of Bose-Einstein condensates beyond the well-known grand canonical anomaly. We develop a segmented-contour approach for the ideal Bose gas, which refines the saddle-point approximation by including non-Gaussian corrections in the canonical and microcanonical ensembles. The method applies to a broad class of noninteracting spectra, and provides efficient access to condensate fluctuations, higher moments, and correlation functions.
  For a three-dimensional harmonic trap with fixed anisotropy, we find that the ratio of the maxima of the microcanonical and canonical condensate-number variances approaches the theoretically predicted asymptotic value $1-3ζ(3)^2/[4ζ(2)ζ(4)]\approx 0.391$ only extremely slowly with increasing particle number. We also show that ensemble effects are visible in the second-order correlation function $g^{(2)}(x)$ near the condensation crossover. After ballistic release from a three-dimensional harmonic trap, the time evolution of $g^{(2)}(x)$ preserves the differences between statistical ensembles.

title: Scattering amplitudes from geometry of kernel-free functionals on piecewise random null paths with memory
summary: We introduce a simple functional of algebra-valued fields with definite Lorentz properties that is kernel-free yet it encodes the structure of tree-level scattering amplitudes. The fields are evaluated at the points of a piece-wise straight paths in the anti-self-dual plane of complexified Minkowski space, with the directions of consecutive segments correlated so that the path has a velocity memory. We show that momentum-space reduction of the functional generates the cyclic Parke--Taylor factor, off shell in terms of light-front bilinears and on shell in terms of spinor brackets. The same reduction, organized differently, can be naturally promoted to twistor space without any twistor-space input: a closed cyclic chain of Penrose transforms on a twistor line, in which the Parke--Taylor denominators arise as boundary terms of the integrals along the paths. Finally we show that derivatives with respect to one of the path parameter generate numerators that together with the Parke-Taylor denominator build scattering amplitudes. Lorentz invariance fixes the spins of the inserted fields and the homogeneities of the corresponding twistor functions without any use of supersymmetry. The three-point outputs reproduce the kinematic forms of the light-cone cubic vertices of chiral higher-spin theory, and the derivative monomials of order four generate the components of the $\overline{\rm MHV}$ supermultiplet of $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang--Mills theory, off shell and on shell.

title: The Disordered Universe 2025: Analytic Properties of Amplitudes and Correlators
comment: 64 Pages, 24 Figures, 2 Tables. A chapter to be published by Springer Lecture Notes in Physics
summary: These lectures provide an introduction to modern techniques for studying the analytic properties of loop-level scattering amplitudes and correlation functions in perturbative quantum field theory. We begin by developing the ideas behind Landau analysis, which identifies the location and nature of kinematic singularities in Feynman integrals (the universal building blocks that contribute to perturbative amplitudes and correlators). We then show how fundamental principles such as unitarity and causality constrain the analytic structure of Feynman integrals, and develop methods for working out some of these constraints in practice. Finally, we connect these observations to the properties of iterated integrals and their symbol calculus, to show how bootstrap methods can be used to determine the functional form of Feynman integrals from just knowledge of their analytic structure. These notes are based on a series of lectures held during the La Ricotta Summer School "The Disordered Universe 2025" from 21~July to 1~August~2025.

title: Genesis in Minimally Modified Gravity
summary: We construct a Genesis scenario within the framework of a type-II minimally modified gravity. The background solution is past geodesically complete and approaches Minkowski spacetime in the asymptotic past. While the Hubble expansion rate grows, the matter sector satisfies the null-energy condition. Scalar perturbations are ghost-free and have no ultraviolet gradient instability, although the squared sound speed $c_\mathcal{R}^2$ becomes negative within a finite infrared region in the Fourier space for a finite time interval. Numerical evolution, including superhorizon growth, yields a nearly scale-invariant, slightly red-tilted scalar spectrum over a broad region of parameter space. The tensor spectrum is blue, with a strongly suppressed tensor-to-scalar ratio. Finally, using the matter fluctuation $δχ$, whose asymptotic normalization is regular, we find that the background-dependent cubic couplings vanish in the far past at fixed nonzero momenta. The surviving matter--graviton and graviton self-interactions are Planck suppressed.

title: Determination of the Magnetic Penetration Depth from Finite-Element Susceptibility Calculations of Spheroidal and Cylindrical Superconductors
summary: The magnetic penetration depth, $λ$, is a fundamental parameter of the superconducting state and is commonly determined from precision measurements of the magnetic susceptibility, $χ$, in the Meissner state. However, extracting $λ$ from such measurements requires an accurate treatment of geometry-dependent demagnetization effects, for which analytic results are only available in a limited number of cases. Here we present a finite-element analysis of the magnetic response of three dimensional superconducting spheroids and cylinders with finite penetration depth. By calculating the magnetic moment and susceptibility, $χ(λ)$, over a wide range of aspect ratios, we quantify the shape-dependent Meissner response and extract effective demagnetization factors in the $λ\rightarrow 0$ limit. For small but finite $λ$, we further determine effective sample dimensions from the initial variation of $χ(λ)$ and propose an improved analytical expression for these. Our results provide a high-precision procedure for determining $λ$ from volume-exclusion based susceptibility measurements and should be directly applicable to the characterization of novel superconducting materials.

title: On 2-loop AdS$_2$ superstring partition function in AdS$_5 \times S^5$ and AdS$_4\times CP^3$
summary: We revisit the 2-loop computation of the partition function of the GS superstring expanded near the AdS$_2$ surface in AdS$_5\times S^5$ and AdS$_4\times {\rm CP}^3$, dual to $\frac{1}{2}$ BPS circular Wilson loop in ${\cal N}=4$ SYM and ABJM theories. In arXiv:2601.08809 it was done in AdS$_5\times S^5$ using dimensional regularization and a UV pole was found. Since dimensional regularization is problematic for the GS string, here we use a heat-kernel cutoff instead. Then the contribution of the local path integral measure, proportional to $δ(0)$, can no longer be ignored. We show that it cancels the $δ(0)$ terms coming from the quartic interactions in the action, leaving the square of the difference ${\rm Str}\,E$ between the regularized numbers of bosonic and fermionic modes. The result is thus UV finite, the pole of arXiv:2601.08809 being an artefact of dimensional regularization. If all fields are regularized with the same smearing kernel, ${\rm Str}\,E=0$ and the 2-loop coefficient $f_2$ vanishes, in tension with $f_2=\frac{3}{32π^2}$ in SYM theory. In the AdS$_4\times{\rm CP}^3$ case the same cancellation leaves a finite term proportional to the square of the coincident value of the massless 2d fermion Green's function, giving, ironically, $f_2=\frac{3}{32π^2}$ instead of $f_2=0$ required by localization. This term is the level-zero (string) part of the result of arXiv:2609.14497 for the AdS$_2\times S^1$ M2 brane in AdS$_4\times S^7/\mathbb Z_k$, where it is cancelled by the higher $S^1$ modes, which also remove a finite mass shift of the massless fermion in conflict with the AdS$_2$ supersymmetry. This suggests that the type II string path integral measure should contain an extra contribution, supplied in the IIA case by the parent M2 brane; in the AdS$_5\times S^5$ case it is still to be identified and may resolve the remaining 2-loop mismatch with localization.

title: Quantum hydrodynamics from Nambu's unpublished fluid notes
summary: We develop a quantum hydrodynamic theory based on Nambu's unpublished note \emph{A New Look at Fluid Dynamics}. The kinetic action defines a metric on configuration space and a mechanical connection coupling an observable cyclic deformation to unobserved fluid modes. Tracing out these modes yields a quantum channel for the observed deformation. We establish a criterion for the exact preservation of coherence between opposite momenta and show how nonzero connection curvature prevents this coupling from being removed. The leading quadratic decay of quantum coherence is determined by the prepared quantum state. For two shear flows, we identify an exact noiseless sign subsystem. Introducing additional generating flows cancels the initial residual of the Euler equations while producing nonzero connection curvature, governed by the same kinetic integrals that determine the classical correction. At fixed mean energy, choosing amplitudes adapted to the dominant coupling flow substantially reduces the initial decoherence, even along the direction that cancels the Euler residual. This advantage gradually diminishes under conditional evolution, eventually leading to a crossing of the decoherence curves. Our example shows that a preparation with a smaller initial coherence-decay coefficient can have a larger maximum sampled loss over a finite readout interval.

title: Thermodynamics and phase structure of rotating Hayward-AdS black holes
summary: We use the modified Newman--Janis algorithm to obtain the rotating ``mother'' black hole solution of the rotating Hayward-AdS black hole. We further derive the fundamental thermodynamic quantities of the ``mother'' black hole in the full unconstrained phase space $(S,J,q,α,P)$, and impose the regularity condition $M_1=q^3/α$ to obtain the thermodynamic quantities of the rotating Hayward-AdS regular black hole. This order of operations gives a Hawking temperature identical to the surface gravity temperature and produces the correct response functions of the regular black hole. For $P<P_c$, the Hawking temperature $T_2$ possesses a local maximum and a local minimum, which divides the black hole into small, intermediate, and large black hole branches, and the $P$--$V$ isotherms display oscillatory behavior characteristic of a liquid/gas phase transition. The small and large black hole branches are locally stable, whereas the intermediate black hole branch has negative heat capacity and is locally unstable. Increasing the rotation parameter $a$, magnetic charge $q$, or pressure $P$ reduces the region of the intermediate branch. The $G_2$--$T_2$ diagram shows that the phase structure, in contrast to the standard swallowtail of the Reissner--Nordström-AdS and Kerr--Newman-AdS black holes, is 8-shaped or C-shaped. These two shapes are divided by the characteristic pressure $P_z$. For $P<P_z$, the curve is 8-shaped, corresponding to a first-order small/large black hole transition. For $P_z<P<P_c$, the curve is C-shaped, corresponding to a zeroth-order transition. These results show that the 8-shaped/C-shaped phase structure characteristic of regular AdS black holes persists under rotation, indicating that it stems from the restructuring of the thermodynamic phase space by the regularity condition rather than from spherical symmetry.

title: Physical structure as an organizing principle for universal Hamiltonian learning
comment: 26 pages, 8 figures, 1 table; Supplementary Information (51 pages) included
summary: Density functional theory (DFT) gives the electronic structure of materials, but its cost limits large-supercell calculations and materials screening. Machine-learned Hamiltonians bypass the self-consistent cycle but are usually system-specific; universal ones could cover new compositions and disordered solids. Such models must generalize across chemistry and keep downstream properties physical, while staying inexpensive for large cells. Here we introduce UniTB, a universal E(3) equivariant Hamiltonian representation framework that integrates physical priors rooted in density-functional tight-binding theory with deep learning. UniTB's network, which corrects a prior Hamiltonian, generalizes across chemistry through a mixture of experts routed by that prior and a charge-equilibration head as in self-consistent-charge tight binding. A projection bounds band shifts from the prior, suppressing spurious states and keeping downstream properties physical. We provide the fastest SO(2) tensor-product GPU kernels for the network. The variant UniTB-Flash assembles its prior from two-center tables at $O(N)$ cost for $N$ atoms, against $O(N\log N)$ on a grid. Trained on 29,242 crystals, UniTB reaches a 0.48 meV matrix-element error on nonmagnetic test crystals spanning 68 elements. Without amorphous training data, both models agree with DFT optics and conductivity of amorphous Ge-Sb-Te. UniTB-Flash ranks candidates with no significant difference from UniTB, whose property values are more accurate; together they screen 16,195 crystals for five application domains of industrial relevance.

title: The Disordered Universe 2025: Features in a $Λ>0$ Universe
summary: A complete understanding of cosmology, from its earliest epoch all the way to the current dark energy dominated era, requires the development of a mathematical framework that incorporates quantum features in an expanding universe. Such a framework, alongside a description of the underlying degrees of freedom, is so far lacking. Several of the pertinent challenges and puzzles already arise upon considering even the most idealised model of an expanding universe --- the de Sitter spacetime and fluctuations thereof. In these lectures, we review some elementary ideas of the de Sitter physics, passing through the representation theory of the de Sitter group, aspects of canonical quantum gravity, all the way to attempts in describing quasi-local features. Throughout, we highlight open problems that motivate ongoing efforts to understand quantum gravity and cosmology in universes with $Λ>0$. These notes are based on a series of lectures held during the La Ricotta Summer School: The Disordered Universe 2025 from 21 July to 1 August 2025.

title: Growing-time trace fluctuations and self-averaging form factors of Grover walks on random lifts
summary: We prove a functional central limit theorem for trace statistics of Grover walks on random $N$-lifts of a fixed finite connected simple $d$-regular graph, $d\geq3$. All observations are computed from the same random lift. The squared centred traces, divided by their observation times, have averages converging in probability to a degree-dependent constant. Their partial sums, centred at this constant and divided by the square root of the window length, converge to Brownian motion. For a window of length $M$ beginning at $t\geq1$, it suffices that $M\to\infty$ and $R^4(d-1)^R/N\to0$, where $R=t+M$. The initial time may remain fixed, with no further restriction on $M/t$. Convergence holds jointly with fixed low-degree polynomial trace statistics; their limiting vector is independent of the Brownian motion. For non-bipartite bases, we also identify Gaussian trace limits at fixed time offsets. Under common initial-time normalisation, subtracting a deterministic growth profile gives an explicit Brownian time change when $M/t$ has a finite limit. Bipartite bases retain the same averaged constant and have twice the Brownian variance rate. The proof combines a growing-dimensional Poisson approximation, a uniform bilinear Chebyshev-energy estimate, a time-decaying Poisson--Gaussian coupling, and a Gaussian quadratic-array theorem. Separate moment estimates give expectation-centred versions under an additional sufficient condition.

title: Noether Symmetries in Scalar--Vector--Two-Form Cosmology with a Topological BF Interaction
summary: We study a canonical scalar field coupled to isotropic triplets of Abelian one-forms and two-forms through scalar-dependent kinetic functions and a constant topological $BF$ interaction. By retaining the lapse in the homogeneous reduction, we recover the Friedmann constraint and identify a sufficient domain in which all twelve physical modes have positive kinetic terms and luminal high-frequency propagation. A separate exponential model admits an accelerating mixed solution with $a\propto t^2$, nonzero asymptotic form fractions, and bounded normalized linear perturbations. For the Noether analysis, we choose a quadratic effective potential in flat minisuperspace coordinates and solve the zero-boundary determining equations. The canonical scalar potential is hyperbolic-squared or exponential, rather than a power law in the scalar field. The causal character of the potential coordinate separates three branches: Branch I admits a de Sitter limit, Branch II cannot sustain acceleration on regular future-complete expanding trajectories, and Branch III gives an exact solution with both form sectors active and late expansion $a\propto t^{4/3}$. Comparisons with consistent uncoupled and reduced-field limits separate the form contributions from the scalar-driven acceleration. The $BF$ term changes the finite-time exchange between the form sectors but supplies no direct negative-pressure source.

title: Anisotropic Structural and Magnetic Response in Sm$_2$Ir$_8$Al$_{31}$: Al-Sublattice Reconstruction upon Sm Substitution
summary: Chemical pressure plays a critical role in determining the crystal structures and physical properties of intermetallic compounds. Here, we report the synthesis, crystal structure, and physical properties of Sm$_2$Ir$_8$Al$_{31}$, a structural analog of UIr$_4$Al$_{15}$, in which the smaller 5f uranium atoms are replaced by larger 4f samarium atoms. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals a tetragonal $\sqrt{2}\times\sqrt{2}\times1$ superstructure with space group $P\bar{4}2_1m$, derived from a UIr$_4$Al$_{15}$-like average structure with space group $P4_2/nmc$. Comparison with UIr$_4$Al$_{15}$ shows that chemical pressure from U-to-Sm substitution produces a strongly anisotropic structural response rather than a uniform expansion of the Ir-Al framework. While one Ir coordination environment undergoes only modest changes, the other exhibits substantial local rearrangement. The Al sublattice primarily accommodates these structural distortions, with selected Al sites showing positional splitting, anisotropic atomic displacement ellipsoids, and partial occupancies, resulting in an Al-rich composition of approximately Sm$_2$Ir$_8$Al$_{31}$. Magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal a direction dependence, including a broad anomaly near 50 K for selected magnetic-field orientations. However, the absence of corresponding anomalies in heat capacity, electrical resistivity, and lattice parameters suggests that this feature is more consistent with an anisotropic magnetic crossover than a bulk thermodynamic phase transition. These results highlight how chemical substitution at the f-element site can induce Al-sublattice reconstruction and modify the magnetic response within a closely related Ir-Al structural framework.

title: The Disordered Universe 2025: An Intro and a Vision
comment: 29 pages. It merges introduction and conclusion chapters of a book to be published by Springer Lecture Notes in Physics
summary: The Disordered Universe is a novel research direction that exploits ideas and techniques coming from apparently unrelated research areas, ranging from cosmology to scattering amplitudes in particle physics and disordered complex systems, with the aim of addressing open questions in cosmology at all scales, from the very infra-red (or very late time) to the early universe. This paper acts as a general introduction and vision for a set of lectures delivered at the first La Ricotta Summer School "The Disordered Universe 2025", held from 21 July to 10 August 2025. These lectures involved open quantum systems, analytic properties of scattering amplitudes and correlation functions, foundations and quantum aspects of the de Sitter universe, as well as statistical physics out of equilibrium and spin glasses. While the lecture notes related to each course taught at the school will be published separately and are inevitably devoted to both conceptual and technical aspects of each of these topics, the school was not meant to be a collage of independent topics: the present paper has the purpose of outlining the global vision, how cosmology ends up being a unifier and benefits from both their viewpoint and techniques, how all the concepts and techniques originally coming from these four different areas are part of the same cosmological narrative, why this point of view deserves to be explored, and drawing perspectives for the future. We consider it crucial to build a microscopic theory for the early universe and maybe one that embraces all scales.

title: Dirichlet-Constrained Random Operators and Quenched Reflection Quantum Walks: Tree Spectra and Poisson Criticality at High Degree
summary:
We study spectral limits of random operators whose incident edge weights are coupled by local normalization, and the reflection quantum walks associated with them. At each vertex of a $d$-regular graph, an independent Dirichlet probability vector distributes unit mass among outgoing directions. At fixed degree, the empirical spectral measures of the associated self-adjoint operators converge almost surely on locally tree-like graph sequences. We give a closed-walk formula for every moment of the limiting tree law.
  Our main result identifies two distinct high-degree scales. After rescaling the deterministic expected root spectral law by $\sqrt d$, a weak limit exists if and only if $dα_d^2$ converges in $[0,\infty]$, where $α_d$ is the Dirichlet parameter. The limits range from a point mass at zero through non-semicircular critical laws to the semicircle law. The critical laws admit a Poisson-tree representation with an explicit Bessel intensity. The extended family, including both endpoint laws, provides a first-Wasserstein approximation uniform over positive Dirichlet parameters.
  In the regime $dα_d^2\to0$, the rescaled law converges weakly to a point mass although its second moment remains one. Weighting spectral mass by its contribution to this moment and rescaling again reveals a different family of limits, classified by $dα_d$. These limits have explicit Beta-product descriptions. A quantitative comparison transfers the variance-scale classification to the centered and rescaled inherited eigenphases of the quantum walk.

title: Geodesic dynamics and tidal forces in a quantum-regularized black hole from string T-duality
summary: In this work, we investigate the geodesic dynamics and tidal force effects in neutral and electrically charged regular spacetimes inspired by T-duality. We first analyze the geometric properties of these solutions, including their regular central structure and horizon configurations, and show how the interplay between the T-duality scale $\ell_0$ and the electric charge $Q$ determines the transition between black hole and horizonless geometries. We then study the motion of massive and massless particles through the corresponding effective potentials, examining the existence and stability of circular orbits and the behavior of their characteristic radii. We further investigate the tidal forces experienced by observers in radial free fall, focusing on the behavior of the radial and angular components, their extrema and sign changes, and the location of these characteristic points relative to the horizon structure of the geometry. We show that the T-duality regularization renders the tidal forces finite in the central region and gives rise to different stretching and compression regimes, including a region of simultaneous compression in both the radial and angular directions, while the electric charge modifies the strength and location of these tidal features. Finally, we analyze the evolution of the geodesic deviation vector for two sets of initial conditions. We find that both the T-duality scale and the electric charge tend to suppress the accumulated radial stretching, whereas the angular deformation is considerably less sensitive to the charge. These results show how the quantum regularization induced by T-duality and the presence of electric charge modify the orbital dynamics and tidal response of these geometries in the strong-field regime. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the corresponding classical limits are recovered appropriately.

title: Learning the Chronology of Materials Discovery for Synthesizability Prediction
summary: High-throughput computational and generative approaches are proposing candidate materials far faster than they can be synthesized, making it increasingly important to identify which hypothetical materials are likely to be experimentally realizable. Positive-unlabeled (PU) learning has emerged as a representative framework for synthesizability prediction, yet existing approaches treat experimentally reported materials as a static collection, overlooking the historical trajectory of materials discovery and the diverse practical factors that have driven its progress. Here we introduce ChronoSyn, a chronology-aware machine learning model that jointly learns synthesizability and the relative reporting order of known materials through a shared composition representation. Incorporating discovery chronology provides additional supervision beyond conventional synthesizability labels, improving prediction performance and enabling ChronoSyn to identify experimentally realizable compositions more effectively than baseline models. Applied to approximately 50 million hypothetical compositions, ChronoSyn identifies chemically coherent high-scoring families that include experimentally reported compositions unseen during training. These results highlight the chronology of materials discovery as an informative learning signal and suggest that the path along which known materials were discovered can point the way to those that will be discovered in the future.

title: Two types of hairy black holes in the (3+1)-dimensional $O(3)$ sigma-model
summary: We construct stationary axially symmetric black holes with scalar hair in the gravitating nonlinear $O(3)$ sigma model with a partly negative symmetry-breaking potential. Our results show that it supports two qualitatively different types of asymptotically flat hairy black holes, distinguished by their connection to the corresponding solitonic branches and by the structure of their scalar hair; the type I black holes are connected to the vacuum branch and type II black holes are connected to regular scalaron-supported spinning solitons. The type II black holes have a strongly deformed scalar field structure, with the scalar field taking its vacuum value on the symmetry axis and approaching the anti-vacuum in the near-horizon equatorial region. We analyze their global charges, horizon properties, and dependence on the model parameters, comparing the solutions with Kerr black holes. For sufficiently weak gravitational coupling, the branch connectivity changes: the fundamental branches of types I and II reconnect to form one continuous family, while their corresponding second branches form another. We find that, in contrast to the vacuum-connected type I family, the scalaron-supported type II black holes extend to substantially larger horizon radii while preserving a nontrivial scalar configuration outside the horizon.

title: Asymptotic Analysis of the Biased van der Pol Equation
summary: We perform an asymptotic analysis of the biased van der Pol equation $\ddot{x} - ν\,(1 - x^{2})\,\dot{x} + x = a$, where the dissipation parameter is large $(ν\gg 1)$ and the bias parameter $a$ is a real number between $-1$ and $1$, corresponding to large-amplitude relaxation oscillations along a stable limit cycle. Using an abridged singular perturbation analysis, the period of relaxation oscillations $T(a,ν)$ is obtained that is accurate within $0.1\%$ of the numerical results for $ν\gg 1$.

title: Quasinormal Ringing of a Schwarzschild Black Hole Surrounded by a King Dark Matter Halo: Higher-Order WKB Analysis
summary: We study scalar and electromagnetic perturbations of a Schwarzschild black hole (BH) surrounded by a dark matter halo described by the King density profile. The lapse function can be expressed as $1-2[M+M_{\rm DM}(r)]/r$, where $M_{\rm DM}(r)$ is the halo mass enclosed within radius $r$; thus, the halo affects the geometry through its enclosed-mass function.
